pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, liquidity and refinancing risk are low in the near term. The group holds cash of USD 459 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 917 million, a total of USD 1,376 million (Documentary Fact; financial handoff liquidity table). The April 24, 2026 amendment moved the revolver and the new term loan A out to April 24, 2031 and repriced term loan B (Documentary Fact; business handoff, new debt events). Scheduled principal over the next twelve months is about USD 50.9 million on the indicative schedule, small against liquidity. The indicative profile is back-ended: about 92% of scheduled principal falls in the years ending September 2031 and 2032, which defers refinancing risk but concentrates it.

Second, leverage is moderate and falling, but its quality depends on a management measure. Net leverage was 3.03x and gross leverage 3.44x at July 3, 2026, against 3.23x and 3.63x at FY2025 (Documentary Fact; financial handoff leverage table). On EBITDA before management adjustments, net leverage is 3.37x (financial handoff). Add-backs of USD 76 million in the nine months and equity earnings equal to 7.8% of trailing Adjusted EBITDA sit inside the denominator, and the trailing period spans 53 weeks (financial handoff gaps). The improvement from 3.23x is therefore real but flatters slightly.

Third, cash conversion lags reported earnings. Nine-month operating cash flow was USD 235 million against USD 273 million a year earlier, and free cash flow of USD 213 million includes a net USD 120 million inflow from selling receivables (Documentary Fact; financial handoff). The guidance ranges imply fourth-quarter free cash flow of USD 312 million to USD 362 million against USD 261 million in the prior-year fourth quarter, which had 14 weeks (financial handoff calculation 14; Management Language for the guidance itself). The fourth quarter is therefore the test of whether conversion improves.

Fourth, business risk is anchored by the customer but not by funding. About 81% of FY2025 revenue came from direct U.S. Government contracts and backlog is USD 48.2 billion, but funded backlog is USD 6.2 billion (Documentary Fact; business handoff, customers and visibility rows). Shutdowns in the first half of FY2026 delayed awards and reduced revenue. Revenue fell 2.5% in the nine months and management lowered its FY2026 revenue range while raising the low end of its Adjusted EBITDA range, so margin gains, partly from favorable contract estimate adjustments of USD 83 million against USD 40 million, are carrying earnings (Analyst Interpretation; business handoff, estimate catch-ups row).

Fifth, creditor-control conclusions cannot be drawn. The credit agreement, its amendment, the indenture and the tax matters agreement are not supplied, the amended covenant level is unknown (the only printed level is the pre-amendment 5.00x first lien net leverage maximum, against an indicative 2.13x), and current holdings of the sponsor-linked stockholder, who holds board nomination rights, are not disclosed (Insufficient Information).

cells.text: Global advanced engineering and technology solutions provider; two segments, Digital Solutions (intelligence analytics, space systems, cybersecurity, IT) and Global Engineering Solutions (environmental remediation, nuclear power solutions, platform engineering, sustainment and supply chain)

Sovereign counterparty lowers customer credit loss, but concentrates revenue on federal appropriations; shutdowns delay awards and billing. Implication: liquidity buffer matters more than customer default risk.
9M 2026 revenue 10,205: Department of War and Intelligence Community 5,334, other U.S. Government agencies 2,811, commercial and international 2,060
The U.S. Government share is 80% of 9M 2026 revenue.
Cost-plus limits inflation risk; the shift to fixed-price raises estimate and execution risk on margin. Implication: margin stability is less certain than the FY2025 mix suggested.
Net favorable earnings-at-completion adjustments 83 in 9M 2026 against 40 in 9M 2025; diluted EPS impact 0.27 against 0.13

Cumulative catch-ups lift reported revenue and profit in the period they are recognised. The increase of 43 exceeds the 24 rise in nine-month Adjusted EBITDA (828 against 804), which suggests underlying EBITDA ex-adjustments did not improve; the filing does not say how much of the catch-up reaches EBITDA.
Backlog 48.2 billion at July 3, 2026 (funded 6.2 billion, unfunded 42.0 billion); remaining performance obligations 8.9 billion, about 79% within 12 months

Backlog includes unexercised options and excludes IDIQ task orders not yet issued; the funded share is 13% (calculated). Implication: near-term revenue is well covered, but the long-dated base is conditional.

Management states net bookings of 17.7 billion and a book-to-bill ratio of 1.3x on a last-twelve-months basis; Q3 awards named include about 500 million of the COSMOS contract and a 974 million CMOE II contract after protests were resolved
Management claims; the Q3 release is not a filing. Awards that were protested can be reversed or delayed until resolved.
Prime status gives contract control and receivable rights but also performance liability.

United States 8,001 and international 2,204 in 9M 2026; international was 2,711 in 9M 2025; key allied customers are the U.K. Ministry of Defence, the U.K. Nuclear Decommissioning Authority and the Australian Department of Defence
International revenue fell 19% (calculated), mainly from joint venture deconsolidation (below). Foreign government exposure adds currency and sovereign process risk.

Contracts moved from consolidated to unconsolidated joint ventures; equity method investments 204; equity earnings 73 and distributions received 87 in 9M 2026; consolidated joint ventures that are variable interest entities hold total assets of 315 including cash of 123
Q3 10-Q page:3, page:13, page:23; Q3 release page:8

Revenue falls but profit moves into equity earnings, which are inside Adjusted EBITDA (8.8% of the 9M 2026 figure, calculated) and are received as distributions. Implication: reported revenue declines overstate underlying shrinkage, while cash from joint ventures is not under direct control.
Cost of revenues 89.9% of revenue in 9M 2026 (89.5% in 9M 2025); selling, general and administrative 3.5% of revenue (4.2%); purchases of property and equipment 22 in 9M 2026
Asset-light model: most spend is labour and subcontract cost. Synergy-driven overhead reduction supports margin, and low capital spending supports cash conversion.
Receivables, net 2,553 at July 3, 2026, of which contract assets 1,007 against 902 at October 3, 2025 and billed receivables 1,490; receivable sales programme with outstanding balance sold of 300
Contract assets rely on future billing; receivable sales fund working capital and support operating cash flow, so they are a liquidity dependency (see financial handoff on the net inflow of 120).

Federal shutdown October 2, 2025 to November 12, 2025, and a partial shutdown January 31, 2026 to February 3, 2026; the Department of Homeland Security was shut down until funding passed on April 30, 2026; the company notes NASA's increased focus on insourcing certain activities
Shutdowns reduced revenue in the first quarter of FY2026 (Q3 10-Q page:27) and slowed awards; insourcing could take work from the largest civil space customer.

Cost-plus payments are provisional and subject to audit by the Defense Contract Audit Agency; investigations could lead to repayments, fines, suspension or debarment; none currently expected to be material
Debarment is a low-probability, high-severity event for a company with this dependence on federal contracts.

Management cites nuclear energy, space, critical digital infrastructure and defense modernisation; Q3 awards include over 400 million for advanced nuclear technology and over 1 billion of classified defense awards
Promotional framing; treat as management view. Evidence for revenue effect is in backlog, not in these statements.

runs.text: Strengths. Liquidity (Documentary Fact; financial handoff): USD 1,376 million of liquidity with no drawings on the revolver and the first committed maturity in April 2031. Deleveraging record (Documentary Fact; financial and business handoffs): total debt fell from USD 4,008 million to USD 3,875 million, net leverage from 3.23x to 3.03x, with voluntary term loan payments of USD 722 million in FY2025 and USD 125 million in June 2026 and no dividends or buybacks. Customer quality and visibility (Documentary Fact; business handoff): 81% of FY2025 revenue from U.S. Government contracts, 91% prime contractor revenue in the nine months, backlog of USD 48.2 billion and remaining performance obligations of USD 8.9 billion, of which about 79% fall within twelve months. Asset-light, cost-plus-weighted model (Documentary Fact; both handoffs): 56% of nine-month revenue on cost-plus contracts, which limits inflation risk, and capital spending of USD 22 million in the nine months, about 0.2% of revenue. Lower interest burden (Documentary Fact; financial handoff): cash interest cover of 3.93x against 3.61x, helped by the April 2026 repricing of term loan B to a 1.75% margin.

Weaknesses. Cash conversion (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; financial handoff): free cash flow of USD 93 million in the nine months excluding receivable sales, against a reported USD 213 million; the programme has a maximum of USD 400 million and USD 300 million was sold and outstanding. Earnings quality (Analyst Interpretation; both handoffs): Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,128 million against USD 1,013 million before adjustments; equity earnings inside the measure; a 53-week trailing period; and a rise of USD 43 million in net favorable estimate adjustments that exceeds the USD 24 million rise in nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, which suggests underlying earnings growth was smaller, although the filing does not give the EBITDA effect. Interest-rate exposure (Documentary Fact; financial handoff): about 74% of debt is floating rate, hedged by swaps of USD 1.3 billion that mature through January 31, 2027, and the company puts the nine-month sensitivity at about USD 23 million per one percentage point. Balance sheet composition (Documentary Fact; financial handoff): goodwill and intangibles of USD 7,378 million are 66% of total assets, so tangible equity is negative USD 2,589 million, and creditor value rests on contract cash flows. Revenue and funding conditionality (Documentary Fact; business handoff): funded backlog is 12.9% of total backlog, revenue declined 2.5% in the nine months, and fixed-price work rose to 29% of revenue from 24%. Documentation and control (Insufficient Information; business handoff): no loan documents, ratings or current ownership, so payout capacity, collateral release and covenant headroom cannot be tested; the tax-free merger structure also limits some strategic actions.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The defining transaction closed on September 27, 2024. Legacy Amentum (Amentum Parent Holdings LLC, owned by Amentum Joint Venture LP) merged with the spin-off of the Jacobs Critical Mission Solutions business and portions of the Jacobs Divergent Solutions business in a tax-efficient Reverse Morris Trust. Amentum Parent Holdings LLC was the accounting acquirer and is the predecessor, so statements before September 27, 2024 exclude the acquired business and are not comparable (10-K page:117, page:128). Before the spin-off the acquired business reorganised under a new company, distributed a cash payment of about 911 million to Jacobs, and Jacobs distributed about 80.95% of its shares to Jacobs shareholders (10-K page:6 to page:7, page:128). Immediately after closing there were about 243 million shares outstanding, held 58.5% by Jacobs and its shareholders and 37.0% by Amentum Joint Venture LP, with 4.5% placed in escrow; in March 2025 the escrow was released, 3.5% to the former Jacobs holders and 1.0% to the sponsor stockholder (10-K page:128). Consideration transferred was 3,948 and total consideration 4,032 including a previously held joint venture interest, and goodwill was recognised at 3,004 on final allocation (10-K page:129 to page:131). Status: completed, with purchase accounting finalised in FY2025.

New debt at the Transaction: a seven-year term facility of 3,750 and a five-year revolver of 850 under a credit agreement dated September 27, 2024 with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as administrative agent, plus 1,000 of 7.250% senior notes due August 1, 2032 issued August 13, 2024 into escrow and released at closing. Proceeds of the credit facility were used together with other cash sources to repay in full the prior first lien and second lien credit agreements and to pay related fees and expenses (10-K page:145, page:149). The filing does not state a sources-and-uses split, so how much of the borrowing funded the 911 payment to Jacobs is Not supplied. An equity contribution of 235 from the legacy equityholder immediately before the Transaction is disclosed (10-K page:153).

Later debt events. In FY2025 the company made voluntary term loan payments of about 191 (June 27, 2025), 250 (July 31, 2025) and 281 (September 30, 2025), together 722, after selling the Rapid Solutions hardware and product business, part of Digital Solutions, to Lockheed Martin Corporation on June 26, 2025 for 360 in cash (10-K page:98, page:105, page:132, page:145). On April 24, 2026 a first amendment to the credit facility (executed; the amendment itself is not in the pack) created a 1,400 term loan A due April 24, 2031, amended the existing term loan into a 1,591 term loan B due September 27, 2031 on lower margins, and raised the revolver by 150 to 1,000 with maturity April 24, 2031 (Q2 10-Q page:17; Q3 10-Q page:11 to page:12). The Q2 2026 release headline describes the term loan A proceeds as used to repay and reprice term loan B (management language, Q2 release page:1). A further voluntary 125 payment on term loan B was made on June 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:12). Subsequent to the quarter end, only the August 10, 2026 earnings release (updated FY2026 guidance, with revenue lowered and Adjusted EBITDA low end raised) and the August 11, 2026 filing are in the pack; no later debt transaction is evidenced up to the cutoff. Sponsor: the filing refers to the equityholder and its affiliates as private equity firms (10-K page:70) but the context names no sponsor and the consulting agreement partners American Securities LLC and Lindsay Goldberg LLC are named only as former advisers (10-K page:153); this handoff does not infer more.

fields.value: The financial base is usable and the group is moderately levered but liquid. At July 3, 2026 principal debt was 3,875 against cash of 459 and undrawn revolver capacity of 917, and trailing Adjusted EBITDA of 1,128 gives gross leverage of 3.44x and net leverage of 3.03x, matching management's 3.0x. Leverage has fallen through FY2026 from 3.23x net at October 3, 2025, driven by a debt reduction of 133 (a voluntary 125 term loan B payment on June 30, 2026 and scheduled amortization) and a 24 rise in trailing Adjusted EBITDA. Trailing cash interest cover is 3.93x on interest paid of 287, an improvement from 3.61x for FY2025, alongside lower interest paid (175 against 194 in the nine months) and the April 2026 repricing (term loan B margin now 1.75% over Term SOFR, from 2.25%).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three points qualify the picture. First, cash conversion is lower than margins suggest: nine-month operating cash flow of 235 was down on 273, free cash flow of 213 includes a net 120 inflow from selling receivables, and the group is guiding to an implied fourth-quarter free cash flow of 312 to 362 to reach its 525 to 575 range. Second, the earnings base includes equity earnings of 88 on a trailing basis (7.8% of trailing Adjusted EBITDA) and management add-backs of 76 in the nine months (Adjusted EBITDA 828 against company-defined EBITDA 752), so the headline measure is more generous than a plain operating measure; the financial maintenance covenant definition is not supplied. Third, the capital structure is mostly floating and secured: 2,866 of the 3,875 is term loan debt, hedged only by swaps with notional 1.3 billion that mature through January 31, 2027, and the senior notes (1,000 at 7.250%, due August 1, 2032) sit behind the secured facilities. Tangible equity is negative (equity of 4,789 against goodwill and intangibles of 7,378), so creditor protection rests on cash flows rather than hard assets. Revenue is shrinking (nine months 2026 down 2.5%) though margins and backlog (48.2 billion) are rising. Comparability limits: FY2025 had 53 weeks, and the FY2024 base excludes the merged business until September 27, 2024, so FY2024 ratios are not shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Amentum is a global advanced engineering and technology solutions provider to U.S. and allied governments, organised in two segments (Digital Solutions and Global Engineering Solutions). It exists in its present form since September 27, 2024, when the Jacobs Critical Mission Solutions business and parts of the Jacobs Divergent Solutions business were spun off and merged with the legacy Amentum business in a Reverse Morris Trust. Creditors therefore lend to a company that has existed as a combined entity for about two years, that carries purchase-accounting intangibles and goodwill (7,378 of 11,199 of total assets at July 3, 2026), and whose pre-merger history does not include the larger business.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating model is low-capital and contract-based. Roughly four-fifths of revenue is from the U.S. Government, mostly as prime contractor, with about 56% of 9M 2026 revenue on cost-plus-fee contracts that pass through inflation and a rising fixed-price share. Visibility is large in headline terms (backlog 48.2 billion) but only 6.2 billion is funded, so revenue durability depends on appropriations and option exercise rather than signed funding. The principal operating risks the filings describe are budget timing (shutdowns from October 2, 2025 to November 12, 2025 and a partial shutdown from January 31, 2026 to February 3, 2026), contract compliance and audit exposure, joint venture structure changes that reduce consolidated revenue while moving profit into equity earnings, and estimate catch-ups on fixed-price work.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy so far is creditor-friendly: no dividends, no share repurchases in FY2025, debt prepayments from divestiture proceeds and cash, and a stated priority of reducing debt. The weaknesses for a creditor are in control and documentation rather than behaviour: the sponsor-linked stockholder keeps board nomination rights tied to its ownership, the tax-free merger structure restricts some strategic actions, and the credit agreement, its April 2026 amendment, the indenture and the tax matters agreement are not supplied, so capacity to pay out cash, incur debt or release collateral cannot be tested. Evidence on creditor-adverse behaviour (priming, uptiering, drop-downs) is neither found nor testable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The defining transaction closed on September 27, 2024. Legacy Amentum (Amentum Parent Holdings LLC, owned by Amentum Joint Venture LP) merged with the spin-off of the Jacobs Critical Mission Solutions business and portions of the Jacobs Divergent Solutions business in a tax-efficient Reverse Morris Trust. Amentum Parent Holdings LLC was the accounting acquirer and is the predecessor, so statements before September 27, 2024 exclude the acquired business and are not comparable (10-K page:117, page:128). Before the spin-off the acquired business reorganised under a new company, distributed a cash payment of about 911 million to Jacobs, and Jacobs distributed about 80.95% of its shares to Jacobs shareholders (10-K page:6 to page:7, page:128). Immediately after closing there were about 243 million shares outstanding, held 58.5% by Jacobs and its shareholders and 37.0% by Amentum Joint Venture LP, with 4.5% placed in escrow; in March 2025 the escrow was released, 3.5% to the former Jacobs holders and 1.0% to the sponsor stockholder (10-K page:128). Consideration transferred was 3,948 and total consideration 4,032 including a previously held joint venture interest, and goodwill was recognised at 3,004 on final allocation (10-K page:129 to page:131). Status: completed, with purchase accounting finalised in FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt at the Transaction: a seven-year term facility of 3,750 and a five-year revolver of 850 under a credit agreement dated September 27, 2024 with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as administrative agent, plus 1,000 of 7.250% senior notes due August 1, 2032 issued August 13, 2024 into escrow and released at closing. Proceeds of the credit facility were used together with other cash sources to repay in full the prior first lien and second lien credit agreements and to pay related fees and expenses (10-K page:145, page:149). The filing does not state a sources-and-uses split, so how much of the borrowing funded the 911 payment to Jacobs is Not supplied. An equity contribution of 235 from the legacy equityholder immediately before the Transaction is disclosed (10-K page:153).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Later debt events. In FY2025 the company made voluntary term loan payments of about 191 (June 27, 2025), 250 (July 31, 2025) and 281 (September 30, 2025), together 722, after selling the Rapid Solutions hardware and product business, part of Digital Solutions, to Lockheed Martin Corporation on June 26, 2025 for 360 in cash (10-K page:98, page:105, page:132, page:145). On April 24, 2026 a first amendment to the credit facility (executed; the amendment itself is not in the pack) created a 1,400 term loan A due April 24, 2031, amended the existing term loan into a 1,591 term loan B due September 27, 2031 on lower margins, and raised the revolver by 150 to 1,000 with maturity April 24, 2031 (Q2 10-Q page:17; Q3 10-Q page:11 to page:12). The Q2 2026 release headline describes the term loan A proceeds as used to repay and reprice term loan B (management language, Q2 release page:1). A further voluntary 125 payment on term loan B was made on June 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:12). Subsequent to the quarter end, only the August 10, 2026 earnings release (updated FY2026 guidance, with revenue lowered and Adjusted EBITDA low end raised) and the August 11, 2026 filing are in the pack; no later debt transaction is evidenced up to the cutoff. Sponsor: the filing refers to the equityholder and its affiliates as private equity firms (10-K page:70) but the context names no sponsor and the consulting agreement partners American Securities LLC and Lindsay Goldberg LLC are named only as former advisers (10-K page:153); this handoff does not infer more.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation has prioritised debt: cash from the Rapid Solutions sale and operations funded 722 of voluntary term loan payments in FY2025, and a further 125 was paid in FY2026, with no dividend or buyback (see above). The leverage effect is in the financial handoff (net leverage 3.23x at October 3, 2025 and 3.03x at July 3, 2026). The business strategy states reliance in part on acquisitions and strategic investments to sustain growth, as well as targeted divestitures (10-K page:23 risk factor list); one acquisition-related cash outflow (70, the working capital settlement for the Transaction) and one divestiture occurred in FY2025 (10-K page:116, page:130), and 9M 2026 shows no acquisition spend (Q3 10-Q page:4). No acquisition appetite is inferred from these. Contributions to equity method investments were 53 in 9M 2026 against 36 in 9M 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:4), a use of cash that supports the joint venture strategy. Disclosure quality is high for the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, net leverage and segment data, but monitoring lacks: the current debt schedule (no maturity table at July 3, 2026), the credit agreement covenant certificate and definitions, and an add-back bridge to the covenant definition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: 81% of revenue from direct U.S. Government contracts, backlog of 48.2 billion with 6.2 billion funded (10-K page:8; Q3 10-Q page:27). Risk mechanic: customer credit risk is minimal, but appropriations delays, continuing resolutions and shutdowns defer awards, billing and cash collection; unfunded backlog converts only as funding arrives. Credit implication: debt service risk comes from timing and liquidity, not demand collapse; a liquidity cushion of 1,376 at July 3, 2026 (financial handoff) is the relevant mitigant. Counter: the rating-statement conflict does not affect this.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: fixed-price share rose to 29% of 9M 2026 revenue from 24% in FY2025, and net favorable estimate adjustments of 83 against 40 (Q3 10-Q page:8, page:27). Risk mechanic: fixed-price work carries cost overrun risk and catch-up adjustments move reported profit between periods. Credit implication: Adjusted EBITDA of 1,128 on a trailing basis may include non-recurring catch-up benefit; leverage of 3.44x gross and 3.03x net is more sensitive to margin slippage than the headline suggests. Counter: cost-plus work remains 56% of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Concentration. Evidence: Department of War and Intelligence Community 5,334 of 10,205 in 9M 2026, and the U.S. Government at 80% in total (Q3 10-Q page:7). Risk mechanic: shifts in defense or intelligence budgets, contract recompetes, or protests concentrate effects. Credit implication: single-sovereign dependence limits diversification; debarment or a large program loss is a tail risk with the greatest effect on enterprise value and on a collateral package secured by substantially all assets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Sponsor alignment and creditor control. Evidence: no dividends and repurchases, voluntary prepayments, board nomination rights linked to ownership, tax-free merger restrictions (10-K page:24, page:71, page:93). Risk mechanic: a holder with board influence could favour distributions or recapitalisations when leverage falls; the restricted-payment capacity in the credit agreement is not visible. Credit implication: current behaviour supports deleveraging, but the sources do not allow a view on whether the documents would stop a distribution; monitoring should track holder changes and the amended credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Key uncertainties. Evidence: no credit agreement, amendment, indenture or tax matters agreement in the pack; no ratings report; current holdings unknown. Risk mechanic: covenant, priming and payout analysis cannot be performed. Credit implication: conclusions on creditor control are provisional.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Amentum Holdings, Inc. has an adequate and improving credit profile with sound liquidity, but its leverage, thin cash conversion and untested loan documents leave limited room for error. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 1,376 million, net leverage of 3.03x (3.23x at FY2025) and cash interest cover of 3.93x, backed by revenue that is 81% U.S. Government and a backlog of USD 48.2 billion. The weakest point is cash generation: nine-month free cash flow of USD 213 million falls to USD 93 million without a USD 120 million receivable-sales inflow, and guidance implies fourth-quarter free cash flow of USD 312 million to USD 362 million. The outcome turns on whether that cash arrives, on the expiry of USD 1.3 billion of interest rate swaps by January 31, 2027, and on credit agreement terms the sources do not supply.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit view (Analyst Interpretation, confidence Medium). Basis: financial handoff (leverage, cover, liquidity, cash flow tables) and business handoff (customer, backlog, contract mix, financial policy rows). Business risk is moderate: the customer is largely the U.S. Government, which removes customer credit loss but exposes revenue timing to appropriations, and the contract mix is moving toward fixed price. Financial risk is moderate: net leverage of 3.03x and gross leverage of 3.44x on trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,128 million, a floating-rate structure, and cash conversion that depends on receivable sales and on catch-up adjustments. Liquidity is a strength. Confidence is Medium rather than High because the credit agreement, the first amendment, the indenture, ratings and current ownership are not supplied, and because the business handoff judged this synthesis as ready with limitations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thesis (Analyst Interpretation): Amentum Holdings, Inc. is a de-levering, liquid government contractor whose debt service rests on timely federal funding and on cash conversion that has yet to match its reported earnings, with creditor protections that the available evidence does not allow us to test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, liquidity and refinancing risk are low in the near term. The group holds cash of USD 459 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 917 million, a total of USD 1,376 million (Documentary Fact; financial handoff liquidity table). The April 24, 2026 amendment moved the revolver and the new term loan A out to April 24, 2031 and repriced term loan B (Documentary Fact; business handoff, new debt events). Scheduled principal over the next twelve months is about USD 50.9 million on the indicative schedule, small against liquidity. The indicative profile is back-ended: about 92% of scheduled principal falls in the years ending September 2031 and 2032, which defers refinancing risk but concentrates it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, leverage is moderate and falling, but its quality depends on a management measure. Net leverage was 3.03x and gross leverage 3.44x at July 3, 2026, against 3.23x and 3.63x at FY2025 (Documentary Fact; financial handoff leverage table). On EBITDA before management adjustments, net leverage is 3.37x (financial handoff). Add-backs of USD 76 million in the nine months and equity earnings equal to 7.8% of trailing Adjusted EBITDA sit inside the denominator, and the trailing period spans 53 weeks (financial handoff gaps). The improvement from 3.23x is therefore real but flatters slightly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, cash conversion lags reported earnings. Nine-month operating cash flow was USD 235 million against USD 273 million a year earlier, and free cash flow of USD 213 million includes a net USD 120 million inflow from selling receivables (Documentary Fact; financial handoff). The guidance ranges imply fourth-quarter free cash flow of USD 312 million to USD 362 million against USD 261 million in the prior-year fourth quarter, which had 14 weeks (financial handoff calculation 14; Management Language for the guidance itself). The fourth quarter is therefore the test of whether conversion improves.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, business risk is anchored by the customer but not by funding. About 81% of FY2025 revenue came from direct U.S. Government contracts and backlog is USD 48.2 billion, but funded backlog is USD 6.2 billion (Documentary Fact; business handoff, customers and visibility rows). Shutdowns in the first half of FY2026 delayed awards and reduced revenue. Revenue fell 2.5% in the nine months and management lowered its FY2026 revenue range while raising the low end of its Adjusted EBITDA range, so margin gains, partly from favorable contract estimate adjustments of USD 83 million against USD 40 million, are carrying earnings (Analyst Interpretation; business handoff, estimate catch-ups row).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, creditor-control conclusions cannot be drawn. The credit agreement, its amendment, the indenture and the tax matters agreement are not supplied, the amended covenant level is unknown (the only printed level is the pre-amendment 5.00x first lien net leverage maximum, against an indicative 2.13x), and current holdings of the sponsor-linked stockholder, who holds board nomination rights, are not disclosed (Insufficient Information).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Liquidity (Documentary Fact; financial handoff): USD 1,376 million of liquidity with no drawings on the revolver and the first committed maturity in April 2031. Deleveraging record (Documentary Fact; financial and business handoffs): total debt fell from USD 4,008 million to USD 3,875 million, net leverage from 3.23x to 3.03x, with voluntary term loan payments of USD 722 million in FY2025 and USD 125 million in June 2026 and no dividends or buybacks. Customer quality and visibility (Documentary Fact; business handoff): 81% of FY2025 revenue from U.S. Government contracts, 91% prime contractor revenue in the nine months, backlog of USD 48.2 billion and remaining performance obligations of USD 8.9 billion, of which about 79% fall within twelve months. Asset-light, cost-plus-weighted model (Documentary Fact; both handoffs): 56% of nine-month revenue on cost-plus contracts, which limits inflation risk, and capital spending of USD 22 million in the nine months, about 0.2% of revenue. Lower interest burden (Documentary Fact; financial handoff): cash interest cover of 3.93x against 3.61x, helped by the April 2026 repricing of term loan B to a 1.75% margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Cash conversion (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; financial handoff): free cash flow of USD 93 million in the nine months excluding receivable sales, against a reported USD 213 million; the programme has a maximum of USD 400 million and USD 300 million was sold and outstanding. Earnings quality (Analyst Interpretation; both handoffs): Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,128 million against USD 1,013 million before adjustments; equity earnings inside the measure; a 53-week trailing period; and a rise of USD 43 million in net favorable estimate adjustments that exceeds the USD 24 million rise in nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, which suggests underlying earnings growth was smaller, although the filing does not give the EBITDA effect. Interest-rate exposure (Documentary Fact; financial handoff): about 74% of debt is floating rate, hedged by swaps of USD 1.3 billion that mature through January 31, 2027, and the company puts the nine-month sensitivity at about USD 23 million per one percentage point. Balance sheet composition (Documentary Fact; financial handoff): goodwill and intangibles of USD 7,378 million are 66% of total assets, so tangible equity is negative USD 2,589 million, and creditor value rests on contract cash flows. Revenue and funding conditionality (Documentary Fact; business handoff): funded backlog is 12.9% of total backlog, revenue declined 2.5% in the nine months, and fixed-price work rose to 29% of revenue from 24%. Documentation and control (Insufficient Information; business handoff): no loan documents, ratings or current ownership, so payout capacity, collateral release and covenant headroom cannot be tested; the tax-free merger structure also limits some strategic actions.
